value.summary: For an arbitrary correlated two-letter input law, memorylessness gives the exact decomposition G(P_{X_1X_2})=F(q_1)+F(q_2)-C_out/2. Combining this identity with the accepted pre-averaging Marton-to-input rows, their universal average, the exact threshold T=2L_RTD, strict concavity of the coordinate and sum envelopes, and a binary Pinsker bound proves the accepted necessary windows for q_1,q_2 and Q, the bound C_out<7/160, and |c_in|<7/40. Direct evaluation on the reflected/transposed one-parameter family gives the additional interval 1/8<alpha<5/13. The argument supplies necessary conditions only.
value.title: Marginal-balance and output-correlation pruning proof

value.summary: A dependency-free Python standard-library checker reconstructs the exact directed RTD threshold, verifies the coordinate and sum envelope separations, checks the output-correlation and input-covariance rational bounds, and verifies the reflected/transposed-family endpoint comparisons using directed high-precision interval arithmetic. These checks corroborate but do not replace the analytic proof.
value.title: Directed marginal and correlation pruning verifier

value.summary: For the half-skew BSSC product channel, any finite-auxiliary two-letter Marton law with unnormalized value M>2L_RTD must satisfy q_1,q_2 in (3/8,5/8), and hence in (7/20,13/20), together with 17/20<q_1+q_2<23/20, I(Y_1;Y_2)+I(Z_1;Z_2)<7/160<0.044 bits, and |P(X_1X_2=11)-q_1q_2|<7/40. Within the reflected/transposed family with masses alpha on 00 and 11 and 1/2-alpha on 01 and 10, a gain additionally requires 1/8<alpha<5/13. These conditions neither establish nor rule out a gain and do not give a capacity converse.
value.title: Marginal and correlation pruning for a two-letter Marton gain

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted result derives necessary marginal and correlation constraints for any two-letter Marton improvement, directly advancing the existing multiletter Marton achievability program and its correlation-structure pruning thread.
